title: 17.9.4. ACUTE COLONIC PSEUDO – OBSTRUCTION (ACPO) AFTER C/S:

17.9.4. ACUTE COLONIC PSEUDO – OBSTRUCTION (ACPO) AFTER C/S:

Ogilivie Syndrome:

1/500 delivery 400/year

Parasympathetic underactivity, sympathectic over activity.

10% due to C/Section and pelvic surgery.

Sympathetic: L2 – L5 => inferior mesentric and pelvic ganglion.

Para: vagus + Hypogestic plexus S1 – S4

Risk Factor:

Age

Anticholinergic drugs

Alpa – agonist sympathomimetics

Cells of cajal in colon

Hypokelemia, hypomegnesimea

Gravid uterus – pressure on sacral plexus – risk of ACPO.

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Low grade pyrexia

Leukocytosis

Rising CRP

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

 

Diagnosis:

•CRP –
•TLC –
•K+ - due to secretion in lumen
•Lactic acidosis

CXR: Gas under diaphram

AXR: Cecal dilation

Colonic dilation

Dilated small gut => ileus

Dilated large gut => ACPO

Air fluid levels:

Ileus

Mechanical obstruction

ACPO – 46%

Difference between ACPO and Mechanical obstrution:

•Contrast enema F/B A x R
•CT – 1st line

(CT with contrast abdominal + pelvic)

Cecal diameter > 14cm indicative of perforation.

Management:

Conservative 24 – 48 hours

NPO

NG

Correction of S/E

Fluid correction

Mobilization

48 hours no improvement or

Cecal diameter ing or static

 

Medical Treatment.

Medical treatment:

Neostigmine – 1st line

2.5mg over 5 min

Repeat after 3 hours if no response

S/E:

•Vomiting bronchspasm, Brady cardia hypotension, excessive salivation

Unsuccessful

Endoscopy:

•Colonoscopy + placement of rectal tube
•cecal diameter 9 – 12cm
•61 – 95% success
•Recurrance – 40%

Percutaneus cecostomy – cecal tube percutenuously.

Surgical treatment:

Indications:

Failed medical

Failed decompression

Ischemia

Perforation.

17.9.4. BOWEL INJURY:

0.3 – 0.8%

70% injuries are minor laceration

75% injuries involve small bowel

Early recognition – good out

Delayed presentation with peritonism – high morbidity and mortality.

Presentation:

•Majority are identified @ the time of operation and carry good outcome
•Late presentation can be lethal
-Fever
-Abdominal pain
-Vomiting
-Tender abdomen
-Signs of peritonism
-Signs of sepsis

Management:

•Opinion and input of surgeon
•Small injuries like puncture with needle heals spontenously, it leaks only in case of distel obstruction.

 

17.9.5. FECAL FISTULA

Common site of large bowel injury – sigmoid colon and rectum.

Risk factors:

•Hystrectomy with scarring or obliterated pouch of douglas

•Endometriosis
•Pelvic dense adhesions

Diagnosis:

Speculum examination

Gastograffin enema – to localize the bowel defect

Management:

Colorectal surgeron’s input

Small fistula heals by proximal defunctioning colostomy

Large fistula require surgical correction by resection of affected bowel.

17.9.6. DUTY OF CANDOUR:

Medical professionals have a duty to be open and honest with patients when things go wrong.

Health and social care Act 2008:

1. Regulation 20 is duty of candour

2. Intention is to ensure that providers are open and transparent with people who use services and other relevant persons in general in relation to care and treatment.

3. It also sets out some specific requirements that providers must follow when things go wrong with care and treatment, providing reasonable support, providing truthful information and an apology when things go wrong

4. The regulation applies to registered persons when they are carrying on regulated activity

5. Breach in this duty can lead to prosecution by the care quality commission (CQC).
